services_industries.name: Wholesale Trade
services_industries.employment_trend: Stable; auto parts and food distribution leading subsectors
services_industries.analysis: Motor vehicle and parts wholesale sales rose 6.1% to $14.4B in February 2026.1 Food, beverage, and tobacco wholesale increased 2.9% to $16.5B, while personal and household goods wholesale climbed 2.5% to a record $13.2B.1 Supply chain realignments continue across automotive, life sciences, and advanced materials subsectors, with 75% of Canadian exports destined for the United States.1 The sector maintains no tracked capital projects in the pipeline, reflecting its asset-light intermediary function within goods distribution networks.

services_industries.name: Retail Trade
services_industries.employment_trend: Mixed; grocery and mass merchants hiring, department stores contracting
services_industries.analysis: January 2026 retail sales reached $70.7B (+1.1% month-over-month), with gains in six of nine subsectors; the February advance estimate indicates a further +0.9%.1 Q1 2026 total spending declined 0.27% year-over-year per Moneris transaction data.2 Grocery sales rose 3% YoY and mass merchants gained 7%, while apparel fell 2%, household goods declined 2%, and department stores dropped 8%.3 Consumer sentiment data shows 43% of Canadians plan to reduce non-essential spending, with only 13% expecting economic improvement in the next six months.3 No capital projects are tracked in the pipeline for this sector.

services_industries.name: Transportation & Warehousing
services_industries.employment_trend: Growing; logistics and warehousing expanding with e-commerce demand
services_industries.analysis: Canada's freight and logistics market is valued at USD $116.63B in 2026, with a projected CAGR of 4.45% to $145.05B by 2031.1 Road freight accounts for 60.97% of the market, while air freight is the fastest-growing segment at a CAGR of 5.15% (2026-31).1 The Port of Montreal Contrecoeur terminal expansion will add +1.15M TEUs in annual capacity, supported by a Canada Infrastructure Bank loan of $1.6B.2 The federal government plans to cut interprovincial freight rates for Canadian steel and lumber starting spring 2026.2 WTI at $86.25/bbl and natural gas at $3.05/MMBtu represent direct fuel cost inputs for the sector.3 The pipeline tracks 466 projects valued at $33.0B, led by Surrey Langley Skytrain ($6.0B), Fraser River Tunnel ($4.1B), and Roberts Bank Terminal 2 ($3.5B).3

services_industries.name: Information & Cultural Industries
services_industries.employment_trend: Growing; AI and cloud infrastructure driving demand
services_industries.analysis: Canada's telecom MNO market is valued at USD $52.28B in 2026, with a projected CAGR of 4.65% to $65.59B by 2031.1 Operators invested $64B+ in network infrastructure over the past five years, achieving 5G coverage exceeding 85% of the population.2 Revenue and subscriber growth are slowing as population growth decelerates, leading operators to moderate network investment.1 The AI Sovereign Compute Infrastructure Program allocates approximately $890M over seven years starting 2026-27 for supercomputing capacity.3 Microsoft committed $19B to Canada (2023-2027) for cloud and AI infrastructure.4 The pipeline tracks 34 projects valued at $727M, primarily in research and innovation facilities.3

services_industries.name: Finance & Insurance
services_industries.employment_trend: Stable; wealth management and capital markets hiring
services_industries.analysis: The Big Six banks all exceeded Q1 2026 estimates. RBC posted record net income of $5.8B (+13% YoY), TD reported $4.04B (+45%), CIBC earned $3.1B, BMO $2.5B, and National Bank $1.25B.1 Wealth management and capital markets divisions drove profits across the sector.1 2026 represents the final year of the five-year mortgage renewal cycle from 2021, with BoC holding at 2.25%.2 Gold at $4,572/oz supports wealth management asset valuations.2 P&C insurers face claims inflation pressure, particularly in auto insurance; OSFI flags softening commercial lines.3 The sector maintains no tracked capital projects, reflecting its financial intermediary function.

sources.title: Globe and Mail — Big Six Earnings

services_industries.name: Real Estate & Rental/Leasing
services_industries.employment_trend: Mixed; industrial absorption recovering, office leasing stabilizing
services_industries.analysis: National office vacancy stands at 13.6% in Q1 2026, down 1 percentage point year-over-year; industrial vacancy sits at 3.5%, marking the first national decline since 2022.1 This represents the first simultaneous office and industrial vacancy decline since 2020.1 CRE investment is forecast at approximately $56B in 2026 (+8% from ~$47B in 2025), with 97% of market participants expecting activity to increase or remain stable.2 Industrial net absorption is forecast to rebound to 20M+ sq ft in 2026.2 2025 was the first year with more purpose-built rentals under construction than condos or single-family homes; asking rents are falling in every major city except Edmonton.3 BoC at 2.25% and lumber at $339/MBF form key financing and construction cost inputs.3 The pipeline tracks 230 projects valued at $59.4B, led by Lougheed Town Centre ($7.0B) and Taza Mixed Use ($4.5B).3

services_industries.name: Professional, Scientific & Technical Services
services_industries.employment_trend: Growing; AI adoption and digital transformation driving consulting demand
services_industries.analysis: AI adoption, cybersecurity, data management, and digital transformation are driving consulting demand across multiple end markets.1 Toronto remains the largest consulting hub in Canada, with energy, finance, healthcare, and technology sectors generating the bulk of advisory engagements for digital transformation and sustainability strategies.1 The sector functions as a service layer to capital-intensive industries tracked in the pipeline. No standalone capital projects are tracked for NAICS 54, though the sector provides engineering, environmental assessment, and project management services to over 3,000 tracked projects across all sectors.

services_industries.name: Management of Companies & Enterprises
services_industries.employment_trend: Stable; concentrated in Toronto and Vancouver financial centres
services_industries.analysis: Brookfield Corporation manages approximately US$900B in assets, while Onex holds ~CA$50B, OMERS Private Equity C$23.2B, and Northleaf ~CA$28B.1 Canada hosts 982 private equity funds, with Toronto (417) and Vancouver (157) as the primary centres.1 Collective investments across the sector exceed $1.94 trillion deployed across 5,300+ portfolio companies.1 The sector functions as a holding and capital allocation layer rather than a direct builder of physical projects, explaining the absence of tracked capital projects in the pipeline.

services_industries.name: Administrative & Support, Waste Management
services_industries.employment_trend: Growing; waste management consolidation driving employment
services_industries.analysis: Canada's waste management market was valued at USD $37.02B in 2023 and is projected to reach $64.22B by 2030 (CAGR 7.10%).1 GFL Environmental is acquiring SECURE Waste Infrastructure at $24.75/share (a 23% premium to the 60-day VWAP), consolidating the industrial waste segment.2 Ontario's extended producer responsibility for blue box services came into full effect January 1, 2026, shifting collection costs to producers.1 The pipeline tracks 25 projects valued at $1.9B, led by the Port Lands Flood Protection project in Toronto ($1.3B), Boat Harbour Remediation in Nova Scotia ($367M), and the Regina Railyard Renewal ($64M).2

services_industries.name: Educational Services
services_industries.employment_trend: Declining enrollment pressure; capital expansion continues in STEM
services_industries.analysis: Ontario allocated $6.4B in additional higher education funding over four years (effective fall 2026), adding 70,000 post-secondary seats.1 Federal international student caps caused a 48% drop in first-semester college enrollment in Ontario in 2025.1 Operating deficits across the sector totalled approximately $338M in 2024-25, with a projected ~$265M shortfall in 2025-26.2 York University suspended enrollment in 18 programs, while Queen's University reallocated 1,200 spots from BA to STEM/professional programs.2 The pipeline tracks 145 projects valued at $5.2B, led by Sage Hills University and Residential Community in BC ($1.5B), UBC Medicine 1 Building ($567M), and UBC Student Housing ($560M).2

sources.title: McMaster News — Ontario Higher Ed Funding

services_industries.name: Health Care & Social Assistance
services_industries.employment_trend: Growing; acute labour shortages persist across all provinces
services_industries.analysis: Ontario's 2026 budget allocates $1.1B+ for hospitals, $9B+ for long-term care, and $64B toward a 10-year health infrastructure plan.1 The province has 147 LTC projects (23,977 new or redeveloped beds) completed, under construction, or approved.1 British Columbia halted construction of 7 LTC facilities while maintaining work on 30 hospitals, 11 LTC centres, and 4 cancer centres.2 South Niagara Hospital raised its final structural beam in February 2026; the 469-bed facility targets completion in summer 2028.1 Ontario allocated an additional $1.1B over three years for home and community care.1 The pipeline tracks 233 projects valued at $20.2B, led by Surrey Hospital ($2.9B), Burnaby Hospital Renewal ($2.4B), and St. Paul's Hospital Replacement ($2.3B).2

services_industries.name: Arts, Entertainment & Recreation
services_industries.employment_trend: Recovering post-pandemic; seasonal tourism employment rising
services_industries.analysis: The Canada Council for the Arts provides grants of up to $100,000/year (three-year maximum) for composite activities, while the Ontario Arts Council offers up to $20,000 for multi/inter-arts projects.1 The sector's capital pipeline is dominated by major resort and recreation developments in British Columbia. The pipeline tracks 143 projects valued at $22.2B, led by Garibaldi at Squamish Ski Resort ($3.5B), Union Bay Estates ($2.0B), and Hemlock Valley Mountain Ski Resort Expansion ($1.5B).2 GDP data for the sector is available via StatCan and ISED industry statistics.2

sources.title: Canada Council for the Arts — Funding Programs

services_industries.name: Accommodation & Food Services
services_industries.employment_trend: Labour shortages persist; industry advocating 33,000 permanent residency spots for TFWs
services_industries.analysis: Canada's hospitality market is valued at USD $21.34B in 2026, with a projected CAGR of 5.18% to $27.46B by 2031.1 The hotel sector posted record occupancy of 65.7%, ADR of CAD $208.71, and RevPAR of CAD $137.17 (+28% versus pre-pandemic levels) in 2024.2 The development pipeline contains 332 hotel projects (45,429 rooms) as of end-2025, while restaurant sales crossed CAD $120B for the first time.1 CoStar projects 1.9% RevPAR growth in 2026 (versus 0.6% for the US).2 FIFA 2026 is identified as a key tourism driver for host cities. The pipeline tracks 2 projects in this sector.2

services_industries.name: Other Services (except Public Administration)
services_industries.analysis: Employment in other services declined 14,000 (-1.8%) in February 2026.1 The sector employs over 500,000 Canadians in auto care alone.1 National right-to-repair legislation is under discussion, while Apple expanded its Self Service Repair program to Canada in August 2025.2 The pipeline tracks 2,345 projects in this broad category, though project values are not individually assigned given the sector's fragmented, service-oriented structure.1

sources.title: Globe and Mail — Right to Repair

services_industries.name: Public Administration
services_industries.employment_trend: Expanding; defence procurement and infrastructure driving public sector growth
services_industries.analysis: The 2026-27 Main Estimates total $502.8B in budgetary spending ($230.4B voted, $272.4B statutory).1 Defence spending increased to 2% of GDP (~$63B in 2025-26), with a target of 5% by 2035.1 The Defence Industrial Strategy mandates 70% domestic procurement, projected to support 125,000 careers and 50% export growth.2 Canada joined the EU SAFE military procurement program ($243B fund) as the first non-EU member.2 Increases in elderly benefits, Canada Health Transfer, and fiscal equalization are offset by the winding down of federal fuel charge rebates.1 The pipeline tracks 194 projects valued at $83.4B, led by Northern Defence and Infrastructure Investment in Yukon ($40.0B), Arctic Defence and Infrastructure in NWT ($35.0B), and Red Deer Regional Hospital Redevelopment ($1.8B).2
